Question:
For order 423, identify the product IDs, aisles, and positions from which to pick the exact quantities needed for each order line, ensuring that the total picked quantity for each product matches the cumulative quantities ordered without exceeding the available inventory in warehouse 1. Calculate the quantities to be picked from each location by prioritizing inventory with earlier purchased dates and smaller quantities, and ensure that picking respects the sequence and cumulative quantities of the order lines for products with multiple entries.

WITH order_requirements AS (
    SELECT order_id, product_id, qty,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY id) as line_num,
           SUM(qty) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY id) as cum_qty
    FROM orderlines 
    WHERE order_id = 423
),
inventory_warehouse1 AS (
    SELECT i.product_id, i.location_id, l.warehouse, l.aisle, l.position, 
           i.purchase_id, p.purchased, i.qty,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
               PARTITION BY i.product_id 
               ORDER BY p.purchased, i.qty, i.location_id
           ) as pick_order
    FROM inventory i
    JOIN locations l ON i.location_id = l.id
    JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
    WHERE l.warehouse = 1 AND i.product_id IN (4280, 6520)
),
requirements_with_pick_order AS (
    SELECT o.product_id, o.line_num, o.cum_qty,
           i.location_id, i.warehouse, i.aisle, i.position, i.pick_order, i.qty,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.product_id ORDER BY i.pick_order) as inv_order
    FROM order_requirements o
    CROSS JOIN inventory_warehouse1 i
    WHERE o.product_id = i.product_id
),
running_totals AS (
    SELECT product_id, line_num, cum_qty, location_id, warehouse, aisle, position, 
           pick_order, qty, inv_order,
           SUM(qty) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY inv_order) as total_picked
    FROM requirements_with_pick_order
)

WITH order_lines AS (
    SELECT order_id, product_id, qty,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY id) as line_num
    FROM orderlines 
    WHERE order_id = 423
),
product_totals AS (
    SELECT product_id, SUM(qty) as total_needed
    FROM orderlines 
    WHERE order_id = 423
    GROUP BY product_id
),
warehouse_inventory AS (
    SELECT i.product_id, l.aisle, l.position, i.location_id,
           p.purchased, i.qty as inv_qty,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY i.product_id ORDER BY p.purchased, i.qty) as rn
    FROM inventory i
    JOIN locations l ON i.location_id = l.id
    JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
    WHERE l.warehouse = 1
),
inventory_ranked AS (
    SELECT product_id, aisle, position, location_id, purchased, inv_qty, rn,
           SUM(inv_qty) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY rn) as running_total
    FROM warehouse_inventory
),
allocations AS (
    SELECT 
        pt.product_id,
        ir.aisle,
        ir.position,
        ir.inv_qty as qty,
        ir.rn as pick_order,
        ir.purchased,
        CASE 
            WHEN pt.total_needed >= ir.running_total THEN ir.inv_qty
            ELSE pt.total_needed - LAG(ir.running_total) OVER (PARTITION BY pt.product_id ORDER BY ir.rn)
        END as picked
    FROM product_totals pt
    JOIN inventory_ranked ir ON pt.product_id = ir.product_id
    WHERE ir.rn <= (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM inventory_ranked ir2 WHERE ir2.product_id = pt.product_id)
)
